faq.title: Questions answered
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about Claude's peak hours, limit changes and promotions.

items.question: What changed with Claude's session limits?
items.answer: Starting March 27, 2026, Claude adjusts how session limits drain during peak hours. During peak hours (weekdays 1pm–7pm UTC), session limits drain faster than usual. Outside peak hours — weekday evenings, nights, and all weekend — limits drain at normal speed. Weekly limits remain unchanged. No known end date for this adjustment.

items.question: When exactly are peak hours?
items.answer: Peak hours are weekdays 1:00 PM to 7:00 PM UTC. Weekday evenings, nights, and the entire weekend are off-peak — limits drain at normal speed during these times.

items.question: What time are peak hours in my timezone?
items.answer: PromoClock automatically detects your device timezone and shows your exact local peak and off-peak windows. The hero section at the top of this page displays your current status in real time.

items.question: Which Claude plans are affected?
items.answer: Free, Pro, Max, and Team plans are all affected. Enterprise plans are not affected because they have dedicated capacity and custom contracts.

items.question: Do my weekly limits change?
items.answer: No. Your weekly limits remain exactly the same. Only the rate at which you move through your 5-hour session limits during peak hours has changed. ~7% of users (particularly Pro tier) may hit session limits they wouldn't have before.

items.question: How can I maximize my session limits?
items.answer: Shift token-intensive background jobs and heavy workloads to off-peak hours (weekday evenings/nights and all weekend). Session limits drain at normal speed during off-peak hours — you get more out of your usage.

items.question: On which platforms does this apply?
items.answer: Session limit adjustments apply across all Claude surfaces: the web interface at claude.ai, desktop apps (Mac and Windows), mobile apps (iOS and Android), Claude Cowork, Claude Code (terminal), and the Excel and PowerPoint add-ins.

items.question: What happened to the March 2026 promotion?
items.answer: The Claude March 2026 off-peak promotion (2x limits) ran from March 13–27, 2026 and ended. The current peak hours system (limits drain faster during peak hours) took effect on March 27, 2026. See the archive section below.

items.question: What is PromoClock and who built it?
items.answer: PromoClock was built by Onur Şendere (@onursendere on X) to help people instantly understand Claude's peak hours and limit changes — and to track verified promotions for 50 popular AI tools in one place. It is an independent project and is not affiliated with Anthropic or any tool listed. Some outbound links are affiliate links; see the affiliate disclosure.

items.question: What happened to the Claude Code +50% weekly limit boost?
items.answer: Anthropic raised Claude Code weekly limits by 50% on May 13, 2026 for Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans. The boost was extended past its original July 13 end date and finally ended on September 14, 2026, when it was replaced by a permanent 25% increase over the original baseline.

items.question: What changed with Claude Code limits on September 14, 2026?
items.answer: From September 14, 2026, standard Claude Code weekly limits are permanently 25% higher than the pre-promotion baseline for Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans. Because the temporary +50% boost ended at the same time, active users have about 17% less weekly Claude Code capacity than during the promo (150 → 125 on a 100 baseline). Five-hour limits and Claude.ai chat limits are not part of this change. Source: @ClaudeDevs on X, August 29, 2026.

items.question: Did Anthropic remove the peak hours system on May 6?
items.answer: Only partially. On May 6, 2026, Anthropic removed peak-hour throttling specifically for Claude Code on Pro and Max plans, alongside doubling the Claude Code 5-hour session limits. Peak hours still apply to Claude.ai chat, Cowork, mobile, and desktop apps for Free, Pro, Max, and Team users — which is why the real-time peak hours tracker above is still useful for most workflows. Sources: Anthropic announcement (May 6, 2026), Ars Technica, Appwrite blog.

items.question: What was the Claude Cowork June 2026 usage promotion?
items.answer: From June 5 to July 5, 2026 (11:59 PM PT), Anthropic doubled the 5-hour usage limit inside Claude Cowork for Pro, Max, Team and legacy seat-based Enterprise users. It applied automatically and weekly limits stayed the same. Free plans and consumption-based Enterprise seats were not eligible. The promotion has ended.

disclosure.metaDescription: How PromoClock uses affiliate links and how we choose which AI deals to list.
disclosure.title: Affiliate disclosure
paragraphs: PromoClock is an independent project. Some links to AI tools on this site are affiliate or partner links. If you sign up or buy through one of them, we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you.

Affiliate relationships never decide whether a deal is listed. We list offers that are publicly available from the tool's official channels, link to the original source, and show the date we last verified each one.
Promo codes are only shown when they are published by the tool or provided by its partner program. Expired offers are removed from live lists automatically.
Tools without an affiliate program — including ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Midjourney — are covered in exactly the same way. PromoClock is not affiliated with Anthropic or any tool listed.
Questions? Reach out on X at @onursendere.

about.title: About PromoClock
about.intro: PromoClock is an independent tracker for Claude's usage limits and for verified promotions across 50 popular AI tools.

sections.title: How we verify
sections.body: Every deal and limit change links to an official source: a help center article, an official blog post or an announcement from the company's own account. We record the date we last checked each one and only publish codes the company or its partner program provides.

sections.title: How often it updates
sections.body: The site rebuilds every day. Deal status is calculated from start and end dates, so expired offers leave the live lists automatically, and the peak-hours clock runs live in your browser.

sections.title: Who runs it
sections.body: PromoClock is built and maintained by Onur Şendere, founder of Digiwings, a one-person digital agency in Shrewsbury, UK. It is not affiliated with Anthropic or any tool listed.
